_comment: Xcode and simulator storage, measured where it lives (AGENTS.md rule 6: patterns are data). Same format as system-storage.json, plus: command = a tool command shown to copy (the app never runs it); perChild = one row per child folder; keepNewest = suggest keeping the highest version per folder. Research: docs/STORAGE-RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 3 (Apple developer forums 84973, 682439, 746361, 842603). Simulator runtime asset names other than iOS are unverified and left out.

entries.title: Device support
entries.why: Debug files Xcode copies for each OS version of a device you plug in. Xcode copies them again when a device on that version connects. Old ones only matter for reading old crash logs.
steps: Everything except the newest version per platform is suggested. It goes to the Trash first.

entries.title: Simulator caches
entries.why: Caches the simulator rebuilds by itself, including its shared system cache. The first simulator launch afterwards is slower.
steps: Safe to add to Cleanup. It goes to the Trash first.

entries.title: Simulator devices
entries.why: Every simulator device with its apps and data. Moving the folder to the Trash leaves Xcode with broken devices.
steps: Run the command to remove devices for runtimes you no longer have, or delete devices in Xcode › Window › Devices and Simulators.

entries.title: SwiftUI previews
entries.why: The simulators behind SwiftUI previews. Deleting the folder by hand has broken Previews for people; Apple's command is the safe way.
steps: Quit Xcode, then run the command. Previews rebuild what they need.

entries.title: Simulator runtimes
entries.why: Whole iOS versions for the simulator, often several GB each. macOS protects them, so only Xcode can remove them.
steps: Remove the ones you don't need in Xcode › Settings › Components.
Or list them with the command, then run xcrun simctl runtime delete with a runtime's id.

entries.title: Xcode archives
entries.why: Builds you archived for release, with the debug symbols you need to read their crash reports.
steps: Delete old ones in Xcode › Window › Organizer › Archives. Keep the ones for versions people still use.

entries.title: Swift package cache
entries.why: Swift packages Xcode and SwiftPM downloaded. They're fetched again when a project needs them.
steps: Safe to add to Cleanup. The next build downloads what it needs.
